newsitem.title: ITALY: Fiat plans hirings to meet hoped for demand.
newsitem.headline: Fiat plans hirings to meet hoped for demand.

text.p: Fiat's cars division plans to hire 270 people at a plant at Melfi in Southern Italy and to transfer 1,000 employees from its Rivalta factory in Turin to the Mirafiori works in the same city, a company spokesman said on Thursday.

Fiat, which is anticipating increased domestic demand following the introduction of a government car sales incentive scheme, wants to boost output of its subcompact Punto and Lancia Y models at Melfi.

The company also said the employees transferred to Mirafiori from Rivalta would be taken out of a state-subsidised layoff scheme. The Rivalta employees would be put to work on producing Punto and Panda models at Mirafiori.
Fiat has ruled out resorting to any temporary layoffs at Mirafiori, Rivalta or Cassino in February.
Unions have said they are opposed to the transfer of workers to Mirafiori on the grounds that it represents a running down of Rivalta's operations.
